authority_current_state.calculation_run_id_authority: Two DISTINCT calculation-run lineages coexist for the same set: (1) simulation_sealed_product_results.calculation_run_id, the per-product/per-simulation-batch run that carries product_market_cost, the outcome distribution, Financial RIP V4, Collector Appeal V5 and Overall RIP V10; (2) simulation_card_variant_pull_rates.calculation_run_id, the per-set card-draw model run that carries price_used and modeled_probability and is the sole input to Chase Accessibility. These are NEVER the same UUID for a given set in the live data. There is no live-table Chase Accessibility snapshot to bridge them (see below).

authority_current_state.supported_set_cohort: 22 sets, all with overall_rip_v10_score populated at price_as_of=2026-08-27 and all with a resolvable simulation_card_variant_pull_rates calculation run. 138 product rows total across those 22 sets.

primary_cohort.coherence_limitation: Financial RIP V4 / Collector Appeal V5 / Overall RIP V10 / product_market_cost all come from the SAME simulation_sealed_product_results row (fully coherent with each other, one row = one calculation_run_id). Chase Accessibility (A_raw, N_HC) is reconstructed from a DIFFERENT calculation run per set -- the most recent simulation_card_variant_pull_rates run for that set_id, dated 1 to 5 days LATER than the Financial/Collector snapshot (2026-08-28 to 2026-09-01 vs 2026-08-27). This mirrors and reproduces the prior architecture-closure finding (docs/research/overall_rip_accessibility_architecture_closure.json), which found a comparable non-same-run offset. No exact same-run coherence exists anywhere in the live data for these two lineages as of 2026-09-01; this cohort is the strongest reproducible substitute and is used as the primary cohort for the entire pass with this limitation documented rather than hidden.
